Food safety and food science now lives within CELS while the Department of Nutrition and Food Sciences is in CHS. CONSTITUTION, BY-LAWS, AND UNIVERSITY MANUAL COMMITTEEReport #2022-2023-15 - SECOND READING OF MOTION TO AMEND THE SENATE BY-LAWSFACULTY SENATE, March 23, 2023 Background and contextIn response to the discussion about preferred modalities of Faculty Senate meetings that arose duringthe Senate meeting on October 20, 2022 and that was included as “Old Business” in the agenda forthe Senate meeting on November 17, 2022, CBUM discussed the issue and with the agenda for theFaculty Senate meeting on December 8, 2022 included for consideration a report with a motion toamend the By-Laws of the Faculty Senate to continue to permit the option of remote participation inFaculty Senate meetings.
During the December 8, 2022 meeting, prior to the presentation of theCBUM report, Senator Preisser moved to eliminate the possibility of remote participation in FacultySenate meetings.
The motion failed.
Subsequently Senate Vice President Nassersharif moved to tablethe CBUM motion to codify the option of remote participation in in-person Senate meetings in theFaculty Senate By-Laws.
A majority of the Senate voted in favor of Vice President Nassersharif’smotion.

In January 2023 CBUM revised the original motion and submitted a new version to FSEC whorequested that the committee draft specific language changes to the By-Laws for consideration by theFaculty Senate.
RationaleIn recognition of the critical role of meaningful faculty engagement in shared governance, CBUMaffirms that it is essential that Faculty Senators, ex officio members of the Faculty Senate, andmembers of the General Faculty actively participate in Faculty Senate deliberations and meetings.
Thecommittee further urges that all members of the university community participate in Faculty Senatemeetings in-person whenever possible, as a matter of cohesion and of maximizing opportunities tosupport and nurture our sense of community.

Although the committee urges in-person attendanceand participation whenever possible, in the interests of equity and inclusion and as a means tooptimize our democratic processes by facilitating the broadest level possible of engagement withFaculty Senate business and participation in Faculty Senate deliberations, CBUM invites the FacultySenate to consider amending the By-Laws to codify the option for remote attendance for all in-personFaculty Senate meetings, with community members, Senators, and ex officio members who attendvirtually retaining all rights afforded to people who are able to attend in-person:- All attendees retain the right to speak and to participate in discussions.- All ex officio members of the Faculty Senate retain the right to make and second motions.- All Senators retain the right to make and second motions, and to vote.
Current language in the By-Laws of the Faculty Senate: 7.3 Regular Faculty Senate Meetings shall be held at least once each month on Thursdays during the academic year.
Proposed changes: 7.3 Regular Faculty Senate Meetings shall be held at least once each month on Thursdays during the academic year.

To facilitate the broadest level possible of engagement with Faculty Senate business, all in-person Faculty Senate meetings shall include an option for remote attendance, with community members, Senators, and ex officio members attending remotely retaining the same rights they enjoy when attending in-person and when attending fully virtual meetings.

State the program objectives.
The Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) undergraduate certificate program for Post Baccalaureate, Pre-K-2 Certification is for those who have completed their undergraduate degree to be certified as a teacher and advance in their teaching profession.
At least 30 hours per week of the incumbent workforce candidate’s active teaching are required; other non-traditional work conditions with RIDE approval can be considered.
The ECCE program will be offered fully online through URIOnline with field experience in the candidates’ own PreK-2 teaching setting, running 7-week accelerated sessions, including a summer session, for 2 years.

The Pathway 2: Undergraduate Certificate, Pre-K-2 Certification requires a bachelor's degree in Science or in Art and to complete pre-professional course requirements prior to admission.
The ECCE program is designed to meet the needs of the incumbent early childhood care and education workforce to access high-quality teaching certificate programs in order to improve teacher quality and student learning.
Aligned with the URI mission, the SOE & CEPS strategic plans, and the Early Childhood Care and Education (ECCE) Strategic Plan for Rhode Island, this program is designed to ensure that the incumbent workforce of early childhood educators has accessible, high-quality, and meaningful pathways toward credential attainment, career advancement, and higher compensation.
This program is supported by The RIDE Educator Pathways Planning Grant.

What is the economic need and workforce data related to the program?

In the State of Rhode Island, in order to achieve a high-quality rating (4 or 5 stars) on the state’s Quality Rating and Improvement System (BrightStars), childcare programs must employ workers with college credits in Early Childhood Education (ECE) and postsecondary degrees.
In addition, childcare programs that seek to become a Rhode Island Pre-Kindergarten provider must employ Bachelor’s degree and Pre-K-2 certified teachers in order to achieve Comprehensive Early Childhood Education (CECE) program quality approval (RI Board of Education, 2018).
A lack of

4 a trained workforce prevents childcare centers from moving up on the BrightStars continuum, from qualifying to become a State Pre-K provider, and from receiving CECE approval.
Furthermore, with the implementation of tiered reimbursement in 2018, childcare programs with higher quality ratings are reimbursed at higher rates by the Child Care Assistance Program.
These higher reimbursement rates will allow programs to increase staff compensation.
More importantly, RI is suffering from a severe shortage in staffing that consequently affects the quality of early childhood teaching and learning in early childhood education (RI Early Learning Council meeting, RI Kids Count report, 2020, 2021).
Our Pathways grant will address this urgent staffing need, thereby enhancing the quality of teaching and learning in early childhood classrooms. b.
